note: Discovery leads for anthropology topic workers (phase 4). LITERACY level: general. NO policy positions; NO advocacy; contested concepts (race, culture, kinship, religion) taught descriptively with attributed sources. All examples ORIGINAL (fictional people/scenarios). Tier A anchors: OpenStax Introduction to Anthropology (openstax.org blocks direct fetch → Wayback captures of canonical URLs; LibreTexts mirror works), American Anthropological Association (americananthro.org), SAPIENS (sapiens.org — anthropology explainer magazine, live), Smithsonian Human Origins Program (humanorigins.si.edu — live, excellent for paleoanthropology), AMNH Hall of Human Origins, PNAS/Nature papers only via verified abstracts (PubMed/PMC). Tier B: Britannica, SEP, UNESCO (for intangible heritage). Registry check FIRST: anthropology may have phase-2/phase-3 content (check content/phase-2/source-registry.json AND content/phase-3 subject workspaces); openstax-intro-anthropology ids may exist. Reuse identical URLs. The sociology subject (phase 4, just completed) minted openstax-intro-sociology-* ids — anthropology's culture/religion/family/kinship lessons must NOT reuse sociology ids for their OWN content; cross-subject overlap is fine as related-topic pointers only.
cautions: Culture/relativism/ethnocentrism: teach descriptively (Boas attribution for relativism); no moral ranking of cultures.
Race as a social and biological concept: per AAA statement (race is not a valid biological category; it is a social construct with real effects); no biological claims; no policy positions.
Human evolution: factually per Smithsonian/OpenStax; no creationist debates; dating figures attributed.
Fieldwork ethics: AAA Code of Ethics attributed; no graphic detail about historical controversies beyond one-line factual mentions.
Kinship/family/marriage: descriptive variation across cultures (Lévi-Strauss, kinship diagrams); no value judgments.
Medical anthropology: descriptive; no medical advice; no treatment claims.
Religion/ritual: described as cultural systems (Durkheim/Turner attributions); never evaluated theologically.
